findings.title: 1. BLOCKING: brokered cancel confirms the worker, not the turn
findings.body: The Windows kill excludes the shared broker and its subtree, but a delivered worker kill makes cancel report `cancelled`. The existing `FAKE_CODEX_IGNORE_INTERRUPT=1` fixture answers `turn/interrupt` while its turn continues; broker socket closure only drops notification routing. The RPC and socket behavior pre-date v1.4.1, but the new Windows kill path turns them into a false cancellation. The same gap affects `workerClosed` after a broker timeout without `turn/completed`.
findings.recommendation: Require a terminal notification for the targeted broker turn before reporting cancellation; otherwise keep it pending and test the ignored-interrupt path.

findings.title: 2. BLOCKING: direct `workerClosed` does not prove descendant exit
findings.body: The marker is written after `client.close()` returns. Direct close, already bounded in v1.4.0, may return at its five-second deadline without child exit; even an observed app-server exit does not establish that its tool descendants exited. If an intermediate parent exits, the 241 orphan walk cannot reach a surviving grandchild. The new marker then lets an empty 241 report pass as proof and cancel return success with an unverified tree.
findings.recommendation: Keep 241 cancellation pending for direct jobs unless the process tree was verified closed; test a descendant surviving app-server exit.

storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

DO-NOT-SHIP: Windows cancel can report success while a brokered turn or direct app-server descendant remains live. This is a source-level review; native Windows behavior was not rerun.

Findings:
- [high] 1. BLOCKING: brokered cancel confirms the worker, not the turn (plugins/codex/scripts/codex-companion.mjs:1368-1377)
  The Windows kill excludes the shared broker and its subtree, but a delivered worker kill makes cancel report `cancelled`. The existing `FAKE_CODEX_IGNORE_INTERRUPT=1` fixture answers `turn/interrupt` while its turn continues; broker socket closure only drops notification routing. The RPC and socket behavior pre-date v1.4.1, but the new Windows kill path turns them into a false cancellation. The same gap affects `workerClosed` after a broker timeout without `turn/completed`.
  Recommendation: Require a terminal notification for the targeted broker turn before reporting cancellation; otherwise keep it pending and test the ignored-interrupt path.
- [high] 2. BLOCKING: direct `workerClosed` does not prove descendant exit (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/tracked-jobs.mjs:231-234)
  The marker is written after `client.close()` returns. Direct close, already bounded in v1.4.0, may return at its five-second deadline without child exit; even an observed app-server exit does not establish that its tool descendants exited. If an intermediate parent exits, the 241 orphan walk cannot reach a surviving grandchild. The new marker then lets an empty 241 report pass as proof and cancel return success with an unverified tree.
  Recommendation: Keep 241 cancellation pending for direct jobs unless the process tree was verified closed; test a descendant surviving app-server exit.

Next steps:
- Fix both proof conditions and run Windows end-to-end checks for ignored broker interrupts and surviving direct descendants.
